title: Install irrigation sprinklers and emitters in landscaped areas

lessons.title: Planning the installation
lessons.html:
Read the plan first

Before you dig, your supervisor will give you an irrigation layout plan. It shows where the pipes run, where each sprinkler or emitter goes, and which valve controls each zone. Lawns and flower beds are usually on separate zones because they need different amounts of water.

Sprinklers or emitters?

ItemUse it for
Pop-up spray headsSmall lawns and ground covers
Rotors (gear-driven)Large lawns and sports fields
Micro-sprayersShrub beds and nursery areas
Drip emitters and drip lineTrees, shrubs, pots and water-wise beds

Drip irrigation puts water right at the roots and wastes very little. It is a good choice in dry areas and where water restrictions apply.

Tools and materials

  • Spade, trenching spade, pick and measuring tape
  • Pegs, string line and spray paint for marking
  • PVC or polyethylene pipe, fittings, risers, sprinklers, emitters
  • Hacksaw or pipe cutter, PVC solvent cement (glue), thread tape
  • Punch tool for drip line, goggles and gloves

Before digging

  1. Ask your supervisor to check for buried electric cables, water and gas pipes, and telephone lines.
  2. Mark the pipe routes with string and spray paint.
  3. Mark each sprinkler point with a peg.
  4. Check that the sprinkler spacing gives head-to-head coverage: each sprinkler should throw water to the next one.
  5. Keep sprays away from walls, windows, paving and roads.

Lift the lawn sods neatly and put them on plastic so you can put them back after the work. Keep topsoil and subsoil in separate heaps.

lessons.title: Installing pipes, sprinklers and emitters
lessons.html:
Trenching and laying pipe

  1. Dig trenches to the depth on the plan (often 200–300 mm for laterals, deeper for mains). Keep the bottom flat and free of stones.
  2. Cut pipe square with a pipe cutter. Remove burrs.
  3. For PVC, clean the ends, apply solvent cement and push the joint together with a small twist. Hold it a few seconds. Follow the product label for drying time.
  4. For poly pipe, use compression fittings and tighten by hand plus a little more.
  5. Flush the pipes with water before fitting sprinklers. This removes soil that would block the nozzles.

Fitting sprinklers

  • Use a flexible riser or swing joint so a mower or foot does not break the pipe.
  • Set pop-up heads level with the soil surface, straight up, not tilted.
  • Adjust the arc (quarter, half or full circle) and the radius so water stays on the lawn or bed.

Fitting drip emitters

  • Lay drip line on the soil surface or just under mulch.
  • Punch a clean hole and push the emitter in firmly.
  • Place emitters at the root zone of each plant. Bigger plants and trees need more emitters, spaced around the drip line of the canopy.
  • Close the end of each line with an end cap or figure-8 closure, so it can be opened for flushing.

Testing and finishing

  1. Turn on each zone. Look for leaks, blocked heads and dry spots.
  2. Fix problems before backfilling.
  3. Backfill: subsoil first, then topsoil. Firm it down. Replace the lawn sods and water them.
  4. Clean up off-cuts, glue tins and packaging.

Safety

  • Wear gloves and goggles when using solvent cement. Use it in open air and keep it away from flames.
  • Never dig before buried services have been checked.
  • Lift with your legs, not your back.

Key points

  • Follow the layout plan and check for buried services before digging.
  • Space sprinklers for head-to-head coverage.
  • Flush pipes before fitting sprinklers and emitters.
  • Drip emitters go at the root zone and save water.
  • Test every zone and fix leaks before backfilling.
